title: Daily Knowledge Tips
description: 365 practical tips covering technology, education, health, safety, productivity, finance and everyday life.

tips.tip: Use Win+L to lock your Windows PC whenever you step away.
Keep important files inside clearly named folders instead of scattering them on the desktop.
Use Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Windows Task Manager quickly.
Use Ctrl+Z to undo an accidental edit in many Windows applications.
Use Ctrl+Shift+S when you want to save a document with a different name or location.
Empty the Recycle Bin only after checking that it contains nothing you still need.
Keep at least one backup of important documents on a separate drive or trusted cloud service.
Restart a computer that has become unusually slow before trying complicated fixes.
Keep Windows and installed applications updated to receive security and bug fixes.
Use descriptive filenames such as invoice_2026_10.pdf instead of names like document1.pdf.
Create separate folders for Documents, Photos, Projects and Downloads to make files easier to find.
Use Win+Shift+S to capture a selected area of your screen.
Use Alt+Tab to switch quickly between open applications.
Press Win+E to open File Explorer quickly.
Review the Downloads folder regularly and remove files you no longer need.
Check the website address carefully before entering a password or payment information.
Use a different strong password for every important online account.
Turn on two-step verification wherever an account supports it.
Never share an OTP, PIN or banking password with a caller, even if the caller sounds official.
Treat unexpected links in messages as suspicious until you verify the sender independently.
Do not trust a message merely because it contains a familiar logo or official-looking language.
Before downloading an attachment, confirm that you were expecting it and know who sent it.
Use a password manager to create and store unique passwords safely.
Review the privacy and permission settings of apps installed on your phone.
Keep your browser updated to receive security fixes.
Do not use public Wi-Fi for sensitive transactions unless you understand the network and use appropriate protection.
Log out of accounts on shared computers after finishing your work.
Check the sender address, not just the display name, when evaluating an email.
Be cautious of urgent messages demanding immediate payment or secrecy.
Report suspicious financial or cyber-fraud activity promptly through the appropriate official channel.
Keep your phone's operating system and apps updated.
Use a strong screen lock instead of an easy-to-guess pattern or PIN.
Review which apps can access your location, microphone and camera.
Remove apps you no longer use, especially those that no longer receive updates.
Turn off Bluetooth when you do not need it in crowded or unfamiliar places.
Use your phone's built-in battery usage screen to find apps consuming unusual power.
Back up important contacts and photos regularly.
Use the official app store whenever possible when installing mobile apps.
Check an app's developer name and reviews before installing it.
Keep emergency contacts accessible even when your phone is locked if your device supports it.
Clean your phone screen with a suitable soft cloth rather than spraying liquid directly onto the device.
Avoid charging a phone under pillows or blankets because heat can build up.
Use the original or reputable compatible charger and cable for your device.
Enable Find My Device or the equivalent tracking feature before the phone is lost.
Review notification previews if private messages might appear on a shared screen.
Start your day by identifying the three tasks that matter most.
Break a large task into smaller actions that can each be completed in one sitting.
Keep a simple to-do list instead of relying entirely on memory.
Group similar tasks together to reduce repeated context switching.
Use calendar reminders for deadlines rather than trying to remember every date.
Keep frequently used documents in clearly labelled folders or shortcuts.
Write the purpose of an email in a clear subject line.
Proofread important messages once before sending them.
Use templates for repetitive letters, reports and routine documents.
Take short breaks during long periods of screen work.
Turn off unnecessary desktop notifications while doing focused work.
Keep a running list of ideas so they do not interrupt the task you are doing.
Finish small tasks that take only a minute or two when they can be safely completed immediately.
Set a specific end time for work when possible to avoid endless task expansion.
Review unfinished tasks at the end of the day and choose the next action for each.
Ctrl+C copies selected content.
Ctrl+V pastes copied or cut content.
Ctrl+X cuts selected content.
Ctrl+A selects all content in the active field or document.
Ctrl+F opens Find in many applications and web pages.
Ctrl+S saves the current document in many applications.
Ctrl+P opens the print dialog in many applications.
Ctrl+N creates a new document, window or item in many applications.
Ctrl+W closes the current browser tab or document in many applications.
Ctrl+Shift+T reopens a recently closed browser tab in many browsers.
Ctrl+Tab moves to the next browser tab in many browsers.
Ctrl+Shift+Tab moves to the previous browser tab in many browsers.
Ctrl+Plus usually zooms in on a web page.
Ctrl+Minus usually zooms out on a web page.
Ctrl+0 usually resets browser zoom to its default level.
Keep one clear header row when creating a simple spreadsheet.
Use consistent date formats throughout a spreadsheet.
Use filters to inspect large lists without deleting or rearranging data.
Freeze the header row when working with a long table.
Use formulas instead of manually calculating repeated totals.
Keep raw data separate from summary calculations when building a report.
Use descriptive worksheet names instead of Sheet1, Sheet2 and Sheet3.
Check for duplicate records before preparing totals.
Keep numbers as numbers rather than storing them as text when calculations are needed.
Use data validation lists to reduce spelling variations in repeated entries.
Format percentages as percentages rather than typing the percent symbol into text.
Use SUM for totals instead of adding many cells manually.
Use COUNT or COUNTA when you need to count entries.
Use conditional formatting to highlight values that need attention.
Make a backup before making major changes to an important workbook.
Study a difficult topic when your concentration is strongest.
After reading a section, close the book and recall the main points from memory.
Explain a concept in your own words to test whether you really understand it.
Use spaced repetition to review important facts over several days.
Practice with questions instead of only rereading notes.
Write down questions you cannot answer and return to them later.
Break a long study session into focused blocks with short breaks.
Remove distracting notifications while studying.
Use examples to connect an abstract concept with a real situation.
Teach a topic to someone else; explaining often reveals gaps in understanding.
Keep a simple study log showing what you learned each day.
Before searching for an answer, make your own guess and then check it.
Compare information from more than one reliable source for important topics.
Check who wrote educational material and when it was published.
Create a small glossary for unfamiliar technical terms.
Drink water regularly according to your needs and local conditions.
Include a variety of vegetables, fruits, grains and protein foods in your meals.
Try to keep a consistent sleep and wake schedule.
Take short movement breaks during long periods of sitting.
Wash your hands with soap and water at appropriate times.
Do not ignore persistent or worsening symptoms; seek professional medical advice.
Keep a list of medicines you take and share it with your healthcare professional when relevant.
Read medicine labels and follow the directions provided by a qualified professional.
Keep routine health checkups appropriate to your age and personal needs.
Use sunscreen and protective clothing when spending extended time in strong sunlight.
Maintain good posture and adjust your chair and screen for comfortable computer work.
Take slow, comfortable breaths for a minute when you feel tense.
Make regular physical activity part of your routine if it is safe for you.
Choose water over sugary drinks more often.
Eat slowly enough to notice when you are becoming comfortably full.
Wash hands before preparing or eating food.
Keep raw meat, poultry and seafood separate from ready-to-eat foods.
Use separate or thoroughly cleaned cutting surfaces for raw and cooked foods.
Refrigerate perishable food promptly rather than leaving it out for long periods.
Label leftovers with the date so older food can be used first.
Clean kitchen surfaces regularly, especially after handling raw foods.
Keep knives sharp and use a stable cutting board to reduce slipping.
Turn pot handles inward on the stove where children cannot easily reach them.
Check food packages for damage, unusual swelling or leakage before use.
Store dry foods in clean, dry, tightly closed containers.
Use a clean spoon each time you take food from a shared container.
Do not taste food with the same spoon and return it to the cooking pot.
Keep a simple list of staple foods before shopping to reduce forgotten items.
Measure ingredients when trying a new recipe so you can reproduce the result.
Let cooked food cool appropriately before storing it according to safe food-handling guidance.
Keep emergency exits and doorways free from clutter.
Check smoke alarms regularly according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Keep a basic first-aid kit where family members can find it.
Store medicines and cleaning chemicals out of children's reach.
Do not overload electrical sockets or extension boards.
Replace damaged electrical cords instead of continuing to use them.
Keep matches and lighters away from children.
Dry wet floors promptly to reduce slip hazards.
Use a stable step stool rather than a chair when reaching high shelves.
Keep a torch and spare batteries available for power outages.
Know where your home's main electrical switch and water shut-off are located.
Do not leave cooking unattended when using high heat.
Keep flammable materials away from stoves, heaters and other heat sources.
Test door and window locks periodically.
Keep important documents in a protected place and maintain backups.
Track your regular expenses for at least a month to understand where money goes.
Build an emergency fund gradually if your income and circumstances allow.
Compare recurring subscriptions and cancel those you no longer use.
Review bank statements and transaction notifications regularly.
Never share a banking PIN or OTP with another person.
Keep a separate record of important financial account contact details.
Set spending limits for non-essential purchases when you are trying to save.
Wait before making an expensive impulse purchase.
Compare total cost, not just monthly payment, when evaluating a purchase.
Keep receipts or digital records for important purchases and warranties.
Pay attention to transaction alerts so unauthorized activity can be spotted quickly.
Use official banking websites or apps rather than links received in unexpected messages.
Do not make an investment decision solely because someone promises guaranteed high returns.
Understand fees and charges before signing up for a financial product.
Keep nominee and beneficiary information up to date where applicable.
Keep a digital and physical copy of important travel documents when appropriate.
Check the official source for current travel requirements before a journey.
Keep emergency contact information accessible while travelling.
Share your itinerary with a trusted person for longer or unfamiliar trips.
Arrive early when an airport, station or appointment has strict check-in times.
Keep valuables secure and avoid displaying large amounts of cash in crowded places.
Use licensed transport services where applicable.
Check your booking details carefully before travelling.
Carry essential medicines in their original labelled packaging when appropriate.
Keep a small amount of local cash as a backup where cards or digital payments may fail.
Save important addresses and booking references offline before leaving.
Check weather conditions before outdoor travel.
Respect local rules, customs and protected areas.
Keep children and vulnerable travellers within sight in crowded places.
Do not leave bags unattended in public transport areas.
Carry a reusable bag when shopping.
Switch off lights when they are not needed.
Use energy-efficient lighting where practical.
Repair or reuse items before replacing them.
Separate recyclable materials according to your local waste system.
Never burn plastic waste in the open.
Use water carefully while washing, cleaning and gardening.
Fix dripping taps promptly.
Plant suitable native or locally adapted plants when possible.
Use public transport, walking or cycling when practical and safe.
Choose durable products instead of disposable alternatives when appropriate.
Compost suitable kitchen and garden waste where local conditions allow.
Keep batteries and electronic waste out of ordinary household garbage.
Carry a refillable water bottle when practical.
Use natural light during the day when possible.
Choose plants that match the sunlight available in your garden or balcony.
Check soil moisture before watering instead of watering automatically every day.
Water plants near the soil rather than constantly wetting the leaves.
Use mulch around suitable plants to help retain soil moisture.
Remove dead leaves and damaged plant material regularly.
Use clean pots with drainage holes for container gardening.
Label seedlings so you remember what you planted.
Introduce compost or other suitable organic matter according to the needs of your soil.
Do not over-fertilize; more fertilizer is not always better.
Observe leaves for early signs of pests or nutrient problems.
Use natural pest-management methods where practical before resorting to stronger treatments.
Choose containers large enough for the mature size of the plant.
Rotate containers periodically when plants grow unevenly toward light.
Keep gardening tools clean and stored safely.
Harvest vegetables and herbs at the appropriate stage for best quality.
Listen fully before preparing your reply.
Use simple language when explaining something complicated.
Ask a clarifying question when a request is ambiguous.
Read important messages once before sending them.
Put the main purpose of a message near the beginning.
Avoid writing angry replies immediately; wait until you can respond calmly.
Use bullet points when a message contains several separate items.
Confirm dates and times in writing for important appointments.
Use respectful language even when disagreeing.
On a phone call, repeat critical numbers or names to confirm accuracy.
Do not forward private messages without permission.
Give specific feedback about the work rather than attacking the person.
Say what action you need and by when when making a work request.
Use a subject line that helps the recipient understand the email quickly.
Keep routine group messages concise so important information is easy to find.
Keep your résumé or professional profile updated as you gain new skills.
Maintain a simple record of completed projects and measurable results.
Learn one useful skill related to your work every month.
Keep professional documents in a consistent folder structure.
Confirm project requirements before starting major work.
Write down agreed deadlines and responsibilities after important discussions.
Keep a backup of business-critical files.
Use a professional email address for formal business communication.
Respond to genuine customer questions clearly and courteously.
Track income and business expenses separately when appropriate.
Create a simple checklist for repetitive client work.
Review your pricing and costs periodically instead of guessing.
Protect customer data and share it only when necessary and authorized.
Keep written records of important business agreements.
Ask for feedback after completing a project.
Give every important web page a clear, descriptive title.
Use one clear main heading for the page topic.
Write meaningful link text instead of generic text such as click here.
Compress large images before uploading them to improve page speed.
Use descriptive alt text for meaningful images.
Make sure important pages are reachable through normal navigation.
Test your website on a mobile phone as well as a desktop.
Keep contact information easy to find on business pages.
Use HTTPS for websites that handle accounts, forms or sensitive information.
Check broken links periodically.
Write useful page descriptions that accurately summarize the content.
Use readable font sizes and sufficient contrast.
Do not hide important information only behind hover effects.
Keep URLs short and descriptive when you control the URL structure.
Add structured data only when it accurately represents the page.
Treat AI output as a draft that should be checked before important use.
Do not paste passwords, OTPs or confidential personal data into an AI tool.
Give an AI tool clear context and a specific task when asking for help.
Ask for a structured answer when you need a checklist, table or step-by-step guide.
Verify important factual claims using reliable sources.
Use AI to generate ideas, then apply your own judgment to choose the best one.
Keep a human review step for customer-facing or high-impact content.
Save useful prompts that consistently produce good results.
Break complex tasks into smaller AI-assisted steps.
Ask AI to identify assumptions and possible errors in a draft.
Use AI for practice and explanation, not as a substitute for learning the fundamentals.
Check generated code before using it on a production website.
Back up important files before making major automated changes.
Do not assume an AI-generated image or text is automatically free of legal restrictions.
Use official documentation when learning how an important software feature works.
Give frequently used items a consistent storage location.
Keep a small donation or discard box for things you no longer need.
Clean one small area at a time instead of waiting for the whole house to become messy.
Store cleaning supplies together and safely away from food.
Use labels on boxes that contain items you rarely access.
Keep frequently used documents in one accessible but secure place.
Check expiry dates on medicines and household products periodically.
Clean refrigerator shelves before restocking groceries.
Keep a small household repair kit together.
Photograph important household equipment labels so model and serial information is easy to find.
Create a simple list of regular household maintenance tasks.
Wash reusable water bottles and containers regularly.
Keep cables organized and label chargers if several look similar.
Store batteries so loose terminals cannot accidentally contact conductive objects.
Keep spare keys in a secure location rather than an obvious hiding place.
Wear a helmet that fits properly when riding a two-wheeler.
Always wear a seat belt in a car.
Do not use a handheld phone while driving.
Slow down near schools, markets and residential areas.
Use indicators before turning or changing lanes.
Keep a safe following distance from the vehicle ahead.
Check mirrors before changing lanes.
Do not drive when impaired by alcohol, drugs or severe fatigue.
Use headlights appropriately in low-visibility conditions.
Check tyre pressure according to the vehicle manufacturer's guidance.
Keep important vehicle documents accessible as required.
Give pedestrians adequate space at crossings.
Do not assume another driver has seen you; make your intentions clear.
Keep children in age-appropriate restraints when travelling by car.
Stop in a safe location before handling navigation or messages.
Keep emergency numbers saved in your phone and accessible offline.
Learn the location of the nearest appropriate hospital or emergency facility for your household.
Keep a first-aid kit stocked with basic supplies and check it periodically.
Call emergency services promptly for life-threatening situations.
Do not give food or drink to an unconscious person.
For a serious burn, cool the area with cool running water and seek appropriate medical care; avoid applying ice directly.
If someone is choking and cannot breathe or speak, use appropriate emergency first-aid measures and call for help.
Do not move a seriously injured person unnecessarily unless there is immediate danger.
Learn CPR from a qualified training provider rather than relying only on a written tip.
Keep emergency medical information accessible for children and older family members.
Know the safest exit route from your home or workplace.
Keep a torch available during power failures.
During severe weather, follow official local emergency instructions.
Teach children how to give their name, location and a callback number in an emergency.
Keep important medicines and medical devices ready when preparing for travel.
Set one small achievable goal instead of ten vague goals.
Review what went well at the end of each week.
Turn a mistake into a written lesson rather than simply feeling bad about it.
Read a few pages of a useful book regularly.
Practice one skill repeatedly instead of constantly switching to new skills.
Keep promises you make to yourself as well as promises you make to others.
Say no politely when a commitment would make your workload unrealistic.
Spend a few minutes planning tomorrow before ending today.
Measure progress against your previous performance rather than someone else's highlight reel.
Ask for constructive feedback from people you trust.
Keep a record of achievements you might otherwise forget.
Replace 'I cannot' with 'I cannot yet' when you are learning a new skill.
Use a timer when you want to start a task you have been avoiding.
Make your environment support the habit you want to build.
Learn from people who have practical experience in the skill you are developing.
The Earth rotates once roughly every 24 hours, producing the cycle of day and night.
Water freezes at 0°C under standard atmospheric pressure.
Water boils at about 100°C under standard atmospheric pressure; boiling point changes with altitude.
The largest ocean on Earth is the Pacific Ocean.
The Himalayas contain some of the world's highest mountains.
Photosynthesis allows green plants to use light energy to help make food from carbon dioxide and water.
An adult human skeleton normally has 206 bones, although individual variation exists.
Lightning is a powerful electrical discharge in the atmosphere.
The Moon does not produce its own visible light; it reflects sunlight.
Sound generally travels faster through solids than through air.
Earth's atmosphere is composed mainly of nitrogen and oxygen.
A leap year usually has 366 days rather than 365.
The equator is an imaginary line around Earth at 0 degrees latitude.
A compass needle generally points toward magnetic north, not geographic north.
An octagon has eight sides.
Use a surge protector or suitable power protection for valuable desktop equipment.
Review active sessions on important accounts and sign out devices you no longer recognize.
Avoid leaving a hot phone in direct sunlight or inside a closed vehicle.
Reserve time on your calendar for important work instead of filling every minute with meetings.
Use Win+Left or Win+Right to snap a window to the side of the screen.
Use absolute cell references such as $A$1 when a formula must always refer to the same cell.
Use retrieval practice by answering questions without looking at your notes.
Reduce stimulating screen activity close to bedtime if it interferes with your sleep.
Prepare some washed or chopped vegetables in advance to make healthy meals easier.
Keep a suitable fire extinguisher accessible and learn its correct use.
Use official customer-care numbers from your bank's website or statement rather than numbers sent by strangers.
Download or save important maps and addresses before entering areas with unreliable connectivity.
Turn off the tap while brushing teeth when continuous running water is unnecessary.
Include suitable flowering plants that provide food for pollinators where practical.
When disagreeing, first state the point you agree on before explaining the difference.
Track a few meaningful business measures rather than collecting numbers you never use.
Avoid loading unnecessary scripts on every page when only one page needs them.
Compare generated summaries with source material before publishing them as factual news.
Do not keep boxes and clutter on stairways or directly in front of electrical panels.
Allow extra stopping distance on wet roads.
